jobs.description:
Purpose of your Job

Our Science and Technology team is looking for a Modelling Scientist to advance data-driven drug development through cutting-edge computational approaches.
In this role, you will apply mechanistic models, machine learning, and molecular simulations to predict the stability and behaviour of biopharmaceutical products. You will work closely with cross-functional teams to integrate modelling into experimental workflows and support innovative, model-informed development strategies.

Are you passionate about scientific modelling and pharmaceutical innovation?
Join us and shape the future of computational drug development—apply today!

Your Responsibility

- Act as a scientific contributor in cross-functional research and development projects, supporting the integration of advanced modelling approaches into biopharmaceutical development.
- Develop, validate, and apply advanced computational models to simulate the physical and chemicals stability, as well as the behaviour, of biopharmaceutical drug products.
- Integrate experimental and structural data into predictive modelling frameworks.
- Utilize a range of modelling techniques, including mechanistic models, machine learning approaches, and molecular simulations, to generate actionable scientific insights.
- Contribute to the development of internal modelling platforms, tools, and workflows to enhance scalability and reproducibility.
- Design and execute simulation studies to investigate formulations parameters, degradation pathways, and process related risks.
- Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams including formulation scientists, analytical experts, and business developers to align modelling strategies with project objectives.
- Analyse and interpret complex data to generate actionable insights.
- Translate and present complex modelling outcomes into clear, impactful recommendations for internal stakeholders and project teams.
- Ensure model quality through rigorous validation procedures and documentation, following internal standards and regulatory expectations where applicable.
- Drive continuous innovation by exploring and implementing state-of-the-art computational approaches relevant to pharmaceutical formulation science.
- Maintain up-to-date knowledge of developments in computational modelling, data science, and biopharmaceutical development to ensure the scientific relevance and competitiveness of modelling approaches.
- Contribute to scientific excellence by co-authoring peer-reviewed publications.
- Support regulatory submissions by providing modelling data and documentation as needed.

What you need to succeed

- Master’s degree or higher in Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related field (PhD preferred)
- Formal training or academic coursework in mechanistic modelling, machine learning, bioinformatics, or molecular dynamics is advantageous.
- 2–5 years of experience in pharmaceutical research and computational modelling, ideally with exposure to protein- and nucleic acid-based therapeutics.
- Strong programming and data analysis skills, with proficiency in tools such as Python, MATLAB, or R, and familiarity with modelling and simulation libraries.
- Expertise in mechanistic modelling, machine learning, molecular modelling, or molecular dynamics simulations.
- Solid understanding of biopharmaceutical products, including structure-function relationships, degradation mechanisms, and formulation challenges.
- Experience in integrating computational models into experimental workflows and interdisciplinary project settings.
- Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving capabilities, with a track record of scientific contributions such as peer-reviewed publications or conference presentations.
- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate complex modelling results into clear insights for diverse audiences.
- Fluency in English, both written and spoken.
- Collaborative and team-oriented mindset with a proactive and open approach to interdisciplinary work.
- A passion for scientific innovation, curiosity, and a commitment to staying at the forefront of computational and pharmaceutical science.

Ergänzende Informationen:
Anforderungen an den Bewerber: 
Grundkenntnisse: Modellbildung, Simulation (IT)
Erweiterte Kenntnisse: Molekularbiologie, Arzneimittelinformation, Angewandte Informatik, Galenik, Modellierungs- und Simulationssprache SystemC, KI-Detektoren, Mathematik, Data Fabric
Expertenkenntnisse: Bioinformatik, Programmiersprache R, Machine Learning, Angewandte Mathematik, Biomathematik, Laborarbeiten, Labortechnik, Datenvisualisierung, Data Science, Data Engineering, Quantitative Forschungsmethode
Zwingend erforderlich: Pharmazeutische Technologie, Forschung, Arzneimittelentwicklung, Programmiersprache Python, Analysis

Work Schedule
Standard (Mon-Fri)

Environmental Conditions
Able to lift 40 lbs. without assistance, Adherence to all Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) Safety Standards, Cold Room/Freezers -22degreesF/-6degrees C, Standing for full shift, Warehouse

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher “Molecular Mechanisms of Musculoskeletal Diseases” (m/f/d) (Molekularbiologe/-biologin)
jobs.description:
The position is located at the Department of Trauma and Orthopedic Surgery, University Hospital Erlangen, within the research group Musculoskeletal Inflammation in Traumatology, led by Prof. Jana Riegger-Koch. Our research focuses on the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying musculoskeletal diseases, particularly osteoporosis, impaired fracture healing, and age-related and post-traumatic osteoarthritis. Two central research pillars are the complement system and its role in inflammation and tissue degeneration, and cell fate decisions in response to cellular stress and injury, including differentiation, senescence, and cell death. We aim to translate these mechanistic insights into novel therapeutic strategies for tissue protection and regeneration. More information: www.riegger-lab.de ( https://www.riegger-lab.de/ )

Your tasks

- Contribute to ongoing research projects and (co-)supervise students
- Independently plan, perform, and analyse laboratory experiments
- Optimise existing protocols and establish new experimental methods
- Contribute to laboratory management and coordination of technical staff
- Participate in teaching activities, including practical courses and lectures
- Present research findings at national and international scientific conferences
- Prepare scientific manuscripts and contribute to grant applications

Qualifications

- PhD in life sciences, such as molecular medicine, biology, or a related discipline
- Strong background in musculoskeletal diseases, mitochondria, immunology, and/or molecular biology
- Hands-on experience in cell culture techniques, fluorescence microscopy, molecular biological techniques (e.g., qRT-PCR, siRNA transfection, and others), Western blotting, and/or histology
- Excellent written and spoken English skills

Additional advantages

- Experience in bioinformatics, omics technologies, or single-cell analysis
- Experience in supervising students, preparing grant applications, or working with laboratory animals
- A strong publication record
- German language skills

We offer

- A crisis proof job with all benefits of a collective wage agreement, including a supplementary pension from the Versorgungsanstalt des Bundes und der Länder (VBL), with us as a systemically relevant employer in the public sector
- A small, international research group with an open-minded, collaborative and respectful working atmosphere
- A highly independent position with substantial opportunities for scientific leadership and career development
- A high-impact research field with biomedical relevance, several core facilities and inspiring research consortia
- Support in acquiring third-party funding and developing scientific independence
- Intended grouping, depending on qualifications and personal requirements, in accordance with TV-L
- This is a full-time position, which can also be done part-time in principle

We offer a PhD position in the research group of Dr. Frederik Kotz-Helmer, which is embedded within the NeptunLab led by Prof. Bastian E. Rapp at the Department of Microsystems Engineering (IMTEK), University of Freiburg. NeptunLab is a highly interdisciplinary research environment focusing on the development of novel materials, manufacturing technologies, and processes for industrial applications. Research from the NeptunLab has been published in leading international journals, including Lab on a Chip, Advanced Materials, Angewandte Chemie, and Nature, and has received attention from national and international media outlets such as the BBC, The New York Times, and the Discovery Channel.
Glass is an essential engineering material for applications ranging from optics and photonics to microtechnology and high-performance components. However, conventional glass manufacturing technologies strongly limit the geometries that can be produced and often require complex and energy-intensive processing routes.
Within this PhD project, a novel extrusion-based manufacturing technology for glass will be developed. The approach is based on highly filled thermoplastic nanocomposites containing silica nanoparticles dispersed in a polymeric binder system. These materials are shaped in the polymeric state by extrusion and subsequently converted into dense, transparent glass through debinding and sintering.
A major focus of the project will be the development of thermoplastic nanocomposites with tailored rheological and mechanical properties. Polymer composition, molecular weight, particle loading, particle dispersion, and processing conditions will be systematically investigated to establish relationships between material formulation, flow behavior, extrusion stability, and the geometry of the resulting components. Structured extrusion dies will be used to directly manufacture complex cross-sectional geometries, providing a new route toward continuous manufacturing of structured glass components.
The successful candidate will work at the interface of materials science, polymer processing, rheology, nanocomposites, and glass technology. The project combines fundamental materials research with the development of a new manufacturing process and therefore provides substantial freedom for both scientific investigation and technology development.
Developing highly filled thermoplastic silica nanocomposites for extrusion-based glass manufacturing.
Designing polymer binder systems with tailored rheological, mechanical, and debinding properties.
Developing and optimizing extrusion processes for complex and microstructured geometries.
Investigating the relationship between extrusion parameters, die geometry, material flow, and dimensional accuracy.
Designing and evaluating structured extrusion dies for the continuous manufacturing of complex glass components.
Characterizing nanocomposites and glasses using techniques such as SEM, XRD, FTIR, Raman spectroscopy, rheology, thermal analysis, and optical characterization.
Establishing quantitative material-process-structure relationships for extrusion-based glass manufacturing.
Presenting research results at international conferences and publishing findings in peer-reviewed journals.
